findings.title: Spawn flusher processes are never killed on restart
findings.body: In _ensure_processes_alive the code does `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()`. Processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, i.e. `SpawnProcess`, which is not an instance of the default-context `multiprocessing.Process` (both only share BaseProcess). So the check is always False, the old hung/crashed process is never killed, and _create_process_for_shards starts a second process for the same shards. Consequence: leaked processes, two flushers competing on the same Redis shards and double-producing segments to buffered-segments.

findings.title: Spawn flusher processes are never terminated on join
findings.body: In join() the code does `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.terminate()`. For the same reason as above, spawn-context processes fail this isinstance check, so a hung flusher that ignores the `stopped` flag is never force-terminated. Consequence: join() spins until deadline and then leaks the hung child process, blocking clean shutdown/rebalance.

findings.title: Negative flusher_processes silently disables flushing
findings.body: Flusher does `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`. A negative value is truthy, so e.g. --flusher-processes=-1 yields num_processes=-1, `range(-1)` is empty, no flusher processes/buffers are created. Consequence: segments are never flushed, Redis grows unboundedly and data is lost, with no error. There is no validation clamping the CLI/factory value to >=1.

findings.title: Restart helper leaks old process/thread
findings.body: _create_process_for_shard() calls _create_process_for_shards() which overwrites self.processes[process_index] and self.buffers[process_index] without stopping/killing/joining the previous entry. For the threading (test) mode there is not even an attempt to stop the old thread since `stopped` is global. Consequence: if ever used, duplicate workers flush the same shards concurrently, causing duplicate Kafka produces and leaked threads/processes.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name shards vs shard
findings.body: In SpanFlusher.main the produce timer uses tags={"shard": shard_tag} and segment_size uses "shard", but the wait_produce timer uses tags={"shards": shard_tag}. Consumers of these metrics expecting a single tag key will see split series. The plural key should be "shard" for consistency.
